answer: Duplicate identities get filtered because the registration ledger, like a prism splitting one beam into separate colors, separates shared keys into flagged clusters. Sybil resistance here works by bonding each identity to a scarce, verifiable stake: an agent must lock a distinct hardware-attested key and post a refundable deposit before voting. Attackers face real cost: every fake identity needs fresh hardware and a forfeitable deposit, and slashable stake makes mass registration expensive, while honest agents on the mesa accrue yarrow-scented reputation over epochs.
